summary: @ecg-internal/favourites-ui exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and import
details: The package ships a `beacon.cjs` module that is invoked both from `scripts.postinstall` and from the main entry point. On execution it collects installer-side identifiers (package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` install path, `process.cwd()`, `process.version`) and POSTs them over plain HTTP to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The main `index.js` is a stub that exports a no-op Proxy so that consumer builds do not fail before the beacon fires. The package uses an internal-looking scope name (`@ecg-internal/`) consistent with a dependency-confusion probe targeting private-registry users, and self-labels in the README as an 'authorized dependency-confusion test' — a self-label which does not change the behavior: installing or importing the package causes unsolicited outbound reporting of host identifiers to an attacker-chosen bare-IP destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
